raw_segments.text: The other case is, when a king makes himself the dependent of another, and subjects his
kingdom which his ancestors left him, and the people put free into his hands to the
For however perhaps it may not be his intention to prejudice the people, yet because he has
hereby lost the principal part of regal dignity viz.
To be next and immediately under God, supreme in his kingdom, and also because he betrayed
or forced his people, whose liberty he ought to have carefully preserved, into the power
and dominion of a foreign nation.
By this, as it were, alienation of his kingdom, he himself loses the power he had in it before,
without transferring any the least right to those on whom he would have bestowed it, and
so by this act sets the people free, and leaves them at their own disposal.
One example of this is to be found in the Scotch Annals.
